- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 1-2% below peak for next 5-7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10-14 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1-3%.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5-1.5% per day for next 3-5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 18-day moving average as baseline, then apply sentiment-weighted adjustment (positive sentiment → +0.5%, negative → -0.5%).
